title: Acids, Bases and Salts
seo_title: Acids, Bases and Salts Class 10 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 2)
standard_code: Class 10, Chapter 2: Acids, Bases and Salts
standard_text: Acids, bases and salts: their definitions in terms of furnishing of H⁺ and OH⁻ ions, general properties, examples and uses, neutralisation, concept of pH scale, importance of pH in everyday life; preparation and uses of sodium hydroxide, bleaching powder, baking soda, washing soda and plaster of Paris.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 10 Science worksheets for NCERT Chapter 2: indicators, the pH scale, neutralisation, reactions of acids and bases, and baking soda, washing soda, bleaching powder and plaster of Paris. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: pH below 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral, above 7 is basic.
body_html:
How to think about it

Acids give H⁺ ions in water and turn blue litmus red; bases give OH⁻ ions and turn red litmus blue and phenolphthalein pink. The pH scale runs from 0 to 14: the lower the pH, the stronger the acid; the higher, the stronger the base.

Acids react with metals to give hydrogen, with carbonates to give carbon dioxide, and with bases to give a salt and water (neutralisation). Common salts have everyday uses: baking soda (NaHCO₃), washing soda (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O), bleaching powder (CaOCl₂) and plaster of Paris (CaSO₄·½H₂O).

Example

Salt from sulphuric acid and sodium hydroxide?

metal part: sodium

acid part: sulphate

Answer: sodium sulphate (+ water)

Example

A solution has pH 3. Describe it.

below 7, and far below

Answer: strongly acidic

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a higher pH means more acidic.
  • Adding water to concentrated acid.
  • Mixing up baking soda (NaHCO₃) and washing soda (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O).

faq.q: Why is pH important in everyday life?
faq.a: Our body works in a narrow pH range, tooth decay starts below pH 5.5, plants need suitable soil pH, and antacids treat excess stomach acid.

items.q: What is the chemical formula of blue vitriol?

items.q: What is the chemical formula of limestone?
items.e: Limestone is calcium carbonate, CaCO₃.

items.q: What is limestone mainly used for?

items.e: Limestone (CaCO₃) is used for making cement and quicklime.

items.q: Why must plaster of Paris be stored in a moisture-proof container?
c: it reacts with water and sets into hard gypsum
items.e: CaSO₄·½H₂O + 1½H₂O → CaSO₄·2H₂O.

items.q: Which acid is found in curd?
items.e: Vinegar has acetic acid; lemon has citric acid.

items.q: What is the name for a solution with a pH of 7?
items.e: Pure water is neutral.

items.q: What is formed when carbon dioxide (a non-metal oxide) reacts with lime water?
c: calcium carbonate (a white precipitate) and water
items.e: Non-metal oxides are acidic.

items.q: How is the sting of a bee (methanoic acid) treated?
c: rub on a mild base such as baking soda
items.e: The base neutralises the acid.

items.q: What is used to treat acidity in the stomach?
c: an antacid such as milk of magnesia
items.e: Mg(OH)₂ is a mild base.

items.q: Which ion makes a solution acidic?
items.e: Acids give H⁺ ions in water.

items.q: How is baking soda made?
c: from sodium chloride, water, carbon dioxide and ammonia
items.e: NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ + NH₃ → NH₄Cl + NaHCO₃.

items.q: What is a strong acid?
c: an acid with a high pH
an acid that gives a lot of H⁺ ions in water
an acid that does not dissolve
items.e: HCl is strong; acetic acid is weak.

items.q: Which ion makes a solution basic?
items.e: Bases that dissolve in water (alkalis) give OH⁻ ions.

items.q: What is water of crystallisation?
c: a fixed number of water molecules in a crystal of a salt
items.e: Blue copper sulphate has 5 molecules of water per formula unit.

items.q: Why should water never be added to concentrated acid?
c: the reaction gives out so much heat that the mixture can splash out
items.e: Always add acid slowly to water, stirring.

items.q: What is formed when a metal oxide reacts with an acid?
items.e: Metal oxides are basic oxides.

items.q: Why does tooth decay start when the pH in the mouth falls below 5.5?
c: acid from bacteria dissolves tooth enamel (calcium phosphate)
items.e: Basic toothpaste neutralises the acid.

items.q: Why does baking powder make a cake soft and spongy?
c: heating gives carbon dioxide gas, which makes the dough rise
items.e: Tartaric acid in baking powder neutralises the sodium carbonate formed.

items.q: Why does dry HCl gas not change the colour of dry blue litmus?
c: without water, HCl does not form H⁺ ions
items.e: Acids show their properties only in water.

items.q: Which acid is found in tamarind?
items.e: Tomato has oxalic acid; nettle and ant stings have methanoic acid.

items.q: Which acid is found in the human stomach?
items.e: It helps digestion; too much causes acidity.

items.q: Which gas is used to make bleaching powder from slaked lime?
items.e: Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ → CaOCl₂ + H₂O.

items.q: What happens to the pH of a solution when it is diluted with water?
items.e: The H⁺ ions become less concentrated.
